sections.content: How many people are "newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors"?

30,060 people

were counted on the census as "newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors evaluate and oversee the editorial direction for the style and content of features and stories for broadcasting and for newspapers, magazines, news websites and periodicals.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors", 15% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors" was 16 to 19 years.

  • leisure and sports managers and proprietors
  • conservation professionals

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors" there were more women than men (55.8% compared with 44.2%).

This means "newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 44.2% and women made up 55.8% of "newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors" included:

  • financial accounts managers
  • business, research and administrative professionals (other)
  • catering and bar managers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors", 10.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (74.1% compared with 25.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (74%) than self-employed (26%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Lambeth, this is in the same region of London.
